title: MAINZ BIOMED N.V. 8-K Filing — 2026-04-15
summary: Mainz Biomed N.V. filed an 8-K reporting the sale of next generation colorectal cancer screening intellectual property to an Italian purchaser for $1.25 million on April 9, 2026, with closing expected by April 23, 2026. The company is pivoting from colorectal cancer screening (it already sold ColoAlert IP in March 2026) to focus on pancreatic cancer detection and post-quantum cybersecurity. The filing also addresses a Nasdaq minimum equity compliance issue that was remediated via a $6 million preferred share investment.
key_points: Asset purchase agreement signed April 9, 2026 for sale of Next Gen IP to Italian-incorporated third party for $1.25 million
Closing expected by April 23, 2026, subject to standard conditions including third-party consents and patent deadline extensions
Company previously sold ColoAlert intellectual property on March 28, 2026
Company is winding down colorectal cancer operations to focus on pancreatic cancer detection and post-quantum cybersecurity opportunities
Nasdaq listing compliance issue: stockholders' equity was $641,600, below the $2.5 million minimum required by Listing Rule 5550(b)(1)
Compliance issue remediated via $6 million preferred share equity investment received in February-March 2026
why_it_matters: This is a routine SEC Form 8-K from a small-cap foreign issuer. It contains no information relevant to market structure or macro catalysts. The document is primarily of interest for corporate governance tracking of a non-investment-grade biotech company pivoting its business focus.
important_numbers: $1.25 million (sale price for Next Gen IP)
$6 million (total preferred share equity investment received Feb-Mar 2026)
